title: Lemon Garlic Chicken Thighs
description: Crisp-skinned chicken thighs seared and roasted in one skillet with garlic, lemon and thyme, then finished with a quick pan sauce.
scaleNote: A 12-inch skillet holds about 2 pounds of thighs in one layer. For a bigger batch, use two skillets or finish everything on a rimmed sheet pan.

image.alt: Illustration of chicken thighs in a skillet with lemon, garlic and thyme

ingredients.note: a juicy lemon gives 2 to 3 tbsp

steps.text: Heat the oven to {temp 425F oven} with a rack in the middle. Pat the chicken very dry with paper towels, then season both sides with the salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Lay the thighs in skin side down and leave them alone until the skin is deep golden and lets go of the pan easily, {time 8-10 min}. Lower the heat a little if the fat starts to smoke.
Turn the thighs skin side up. Tuck the garlic, thyme and lemon slices into the gaps between them.

Move the skillet to the oven and roast until the thickest thigh reads {temp 175F internal} near the bone, {time 20-25 min}. Chicken is safe to eat from {temp 165F internal}, but thighs are juicier and more tender a little higher.

Transfer the chicken to a plate. The skillet handle is now very hot, so grab it with an oven mitt. Pour off all but about {qty 1 tbsp fixed} of fat, set the skillet over medium heat and add the broth and lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer until slightly reduced, {time 2-3 min}.
Take the skillet off the heat and swirl in the butter until melted. Spoon the sauce, garlic and lemon slices over the chicken and scatter the parsley on top.

notes: Boneless thighs work too: sear them for {time 5 min} per side and roast for {time 10-12 min notimer}, until they reach {temp 175F internal}.
The roasted garlic cloves turn soft and sweet. Mash them into the sauce or spread them on bread.
Leftovers keep in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
